title: What's Different About Your Dad's Truck, Your Truck and Your Kids' or Even Grandkid's Trucks?
abstract: This presentation prepared for the 2020 Mid-America Trucking Show examines the technological evolution of heavy commercial trucks across generations, contrasting pre-emissions classic trucks with modern aerodynamic models and future zero-emission and autonomous vehicles. It analyzes the financial and efficiency penalties of legacy components like external air cleaners and exhaust stacks, tracks historical diesel fuel price volatility, and discusses the adoption trajectory of emerging technologies including battery electric, hydrogen fuel cell, platooning, and camera-based vision systems to lower total cost of ownership.
key_findings: External air cleaners on older classic trucks create aerodynamic drag costing $1,500 to $2,500 annually in excess fuel at $3 per gallon.
Legacy pre-emissions trucks were roughly 15% less fuel-efficient than modern aerodynamic tractor designs.
Modern emissions controls require 70 contemporary trucks to equal the NOx and particulate matter output of a single pre-2002 truck.
Battery electric trucks are projected to scale from port drayage and regional day-cab routes into long-haul operations as battery technology improves.
Total cost of ownership (TCO) remains the primary driver for technology adoption across fleets and owner-operators.
